title: More Rules, Longer Lists? Benchmarking Self-Evolving Agents on a Hidden-Rule Curriculum
why: CLR-Bench is a curriculum benchmark for self-evolving agents that rewrite persistent state from feedback: tests whether agents learn latent hidden rules vs growing exception lists. Direct evaluation substrate for harness-level self-evolution (ACE/Dynamic Cheatsheet compared).
mechanism: Persistent-state rewrite from practice feedback on a hidden-rule curriculum; probes distinguish rule abstraction from exception-list growth; compares self-evolving baselines (ACE, Dynamic Cheatsheet) across model strengths.

title: TinyAstral: Transferring Self-Evolving Harnesses to Tiny Generalist Manipulation Agents
why: Two-stage RSI: frontier agents propose teacher harness edits accepted only under paired statistical tests, then freeze harness and distill into a tiny student that inherits the self-evolved harness—explicit self-evolving harness transfer for embodied agents.
mechanism: Recursive self-improvement of teacher harness (tools/feedback/memory/recovery) via LLM-proposed edits + paired statistical acceptance; freeze harness; distill teacher trajectories into compact student sharing the evolved harness.
